not_collected: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (excluded)
statement: This observatory reads AI Incident Database (weekly Excel export) and Curated public-sector cases (cases.json). It does not read Find Case Law (UK court judgments) (licence-required); OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (excluded); AIAAIC Repository (unverified); Database of AI Litigation (DAIL) (unverified); ICO enforcement action (covered-elsewhere). Counts describe what these sources recorded, not how often failures happen in the world. Media-sourced incidents are allegations unless an authority made a finding.

sources.name: AI Incident Database (weekly Excel export)
sources.licence: Incidents, classifications and entities are CC BY-SA 4.0. Report text is not licensed and is not collected.
sources.verify_note: Workbook layout read from the project's own export pipeline (site/excel-export-pipeline: Incidents sheet, banner rows 1-2, headers on row 3). The listing page showed AIID_Excel_Export-20261005.xlsx on 11 Oct 2026. The parser finds the header row by name rather than trusting row 3, and the run fails loudly if the required columns are missing.
sources.change_since_july: The read-only GraphQL endpoint the July design used now requires a logged-in account (HTTP 401, API_LOGIN_REQUIRED). The project points bulk users to this export instead.

sources.name: Curated public-sector cases (cases.json)
sources.licence: Facts summarised in own words, with links to primary or reputable sources.
sources.verify_note: Each case carries its sources. Add a case only with a source for every fact, and state the determination level honestly.

sources.name: Find Case Law (UK court judgments)

licence.note: Automated identification or classification of judgments is computational analysis, which the Open Justice Licence excludes. A free computational analysis licence is required. Set granted to true and add the reference only once the licence is issued.

sources.rate_limit: 1,000 requests per rolling five minutes per IP (documented). The collector waits 1 second between requests and fetches at most 300 judgments per run.
sources.determination: determined (a court or tribunal made findings; the AI element may be incidental to the case)
sources.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Justice Licence v1.0.
sources.verify_note: Endpoint and parameters taken from the published OpenAPI spec (nationalarchives/ds-find-caselaw-docs, public_api.yml). Under the nine principles, no judgment text is stored or published: only case metadata, a link to the authoritative version, and the failure-mode labels the classifier assigned.

sources.name: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor
sources.verify_note: No API or bulk download is offered. The terms say the OECD cannot grant rights to reuse the underlying news material, and the site is marked all rights reserved. Read it by hand; do not scrape it.

sources.name: AIAAIC Repository
sources.verify_note: Public website listing. No documented download or licence found on 11 Oct 2026. Ask AIAAIC about reuse terms before connecting it.

sources.name: Database of AI Litigation (DAIL)
sources.verify_note: Highest-value missing source: litigation records carry what happened afterwards. Data access route not yet confirmed; needs its own fetcher.

sources.name: ICO enforcement action
sources.verify_note: The enforcement listing loads its results in the browser and the ICO has withdrawn its RSS feeds. Regulator output belongs in the regulatory horizon scanner (AIRegScanner), which keeps authoritative publishers separate from journalism by design.
